items.title: Reflection AI Beam live on OpenRouter at $0.25/$1 per M tokens — ~10x cheaper than Argon, but Beam's own Terminal-Bench v2.1 of 80.1 lands behind every major open-weight coding leader (GLM 5.2/5.3, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8-Max, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), and no independent reproduction yet
items.summary: Two days after Reflection AI released Beam's weights on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, hosted API access has materialized and the open-weight landscape is becoming clearer. OpenRouter lists reflection/beam-1.0-501b-a23b with 1M-token context, configurable reasoning effort, function calling and structured output. Pricing on the cheapest listed provider is $0.25 per million input tokens and $1.00 per million output tokens; a second provider row shows $0.40/$1.20, and Vercel AI Gateway is listed much higher at $1.30/$4.30. OpenRouter reports 99.96% availability over the last three days, around 134 tokens per second throughput and roughly 0.56s median latency from the best provider. Baseten is also carrying the model, and self-serve API keys from Reflection opened the same day as the weight drop (Oct 16). Community reception: the Hugging Face announcement thread reached ~549 points and ~174 comments on Hacker News within the first few days, with the center of gravity shifting from launch excitement to hardware math — roughly 501 GB of VRAM in FP8 just to load the weights, and about 250 GB at 4-bit. The sharpest new reading is on the open-weight coding leaderboard: Reflection's own revised benchmark table (updated Oct 8, 2026) shows Beam at 80.1 on Terminal-Bench v2.1, which sits below GLM 5.2 (81.0), GLM 5.3 (88.2), Kimi K3 (88.3), Qwen 3.8-Max (86.6) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (90.6) — all vendor-reported figures, but the comparison points are now specific rather than generic. On SWE-bench Pro v1 Beam reports 65.5 against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's 67.7. Reflection's broader performance claims — matching GLM 5.2 at a quarter to a third of the inference compute — remain vendor-reported, and TechCrunch and others have explicitly noted no third party has reproduced them. Artificial Analysis posted on X that it received early access and that preliminary indicators suggest Beam will be one of the most token-efficient open models for its level of intelligence; a formal published evaluation has not landed, and its Intelligence Index entry pre-Beam already placed the model at 30 (#19 of 120). Epoch AI and independent SWE-Bench evaluations are still expected late October or early November.
items.why_it_matters: The am item from Oct 18 flagged OpenRouter as 'where Beam should be appearing this week.' It did, and the overnight read sharpens the picture in two directions worth sitting with. First, the pricing story is now clear and holds up: $0.25/M input and $1/M output on OpenRouter is roughly 8x cheaper than Argon's current introductory API rates ($2 input / $10 output) and 16–20x cheaper after Argon's December 1 price doubling. Vercel AI Gateway's $1.30/$4.30 listing shows that the headline cheap price is route-specific, not universal — if Gabe spins up Beam from a Python workflow, OpenRouter is the route to use, not a generic gateway. The 1M-token context, structured output and function calling make Beam practical from a plain Python script without rolling custom JSON parsing or tool-calling glue. Second, and more useful for setting expectations, the open-weight landscape framing has firmed up. Yesterday's pm already said Beam's Terminal-Bench 80.1 trails 'several competitors'; this morning the specific numbers from Reflection's own Oct 8 revised table make clear it trails every one of the current open-weight coding leaders: GLM 5.2 81.0, GLM 5.3 88.2, Kimi K3 88.3, Qwen 3.8-Max 86.6, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 90.6. On SWE-bench Pro v1, Beam reports 65.5 vs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 67.7. These are all vendor-reported, so caveats apply across the board — but the comparison points are now specific, not generic. Three practical reads for Gabe: (1) The cost argument for trying Beam is still the strongest one. At $0.25/M input and $1/M output, trying it on three or four of Gabe's real HTML/CSS/Python tasks is cheap enough to just do and measure. The right comparison is not against Argon or Opus 5.5, which are reasoning tier; it is against the mid-tier hosted options and the cheaper open-weight APIs via OpenRouter. (2) The 'open-weight frontier for coding' is not Beam right now. If quality matters more than license (which it usually does for a hobbyist), Beam's own numbers point to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 as the stronger open-weight coding options to try first on OpenRouter. (3) Independent reproduction is still pending. Artificial Analysis is testing and has posted a preliminary X comment on token efficiency; Epoch AI's result is expected in a few weeks. Given the 2024 Reflection 70B episode (benchmark overclaims, inflated eval code, API calling Claude Sonnet behind the scenes), it's reasonable to wait on an independent read before trusting vendor leaderboard positioning. For the hobbyist play: pull a key, run three real tasks, compare quality against both Sonnet 5.5 (known-steady output) and one of the Chinese open-weight coding leaders on OpenRouter. The yesterday am's Argon item still points at Sonnet 5.5 as the better default on Gabe's stack via Vibe Code Bench and Code Migration; Beam enters as a cheap option worth measuring against both, but on current numbers it is not the open-weight coding leader to beat.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Beam is cheap on OpenRouter ($0.25/$1) and practical from a Python script, but Reflection's own Oct 8 table puts its Terminal-Bench 80.1 behind every current open-weight coding leader — the open-weight frontier for coding isn't Beam.

takes.source: Reflection AI Blog — Beam is Available
takes.take: Primary source for Oct 16 release. Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face alongside the Beam API. Vendor benchmark table included; Reflection updated the benchmark table on Oct 8, 2026 (table revision, not architecture or parameter count).

takes.source: Unite.ai — Reflection Releases Beam's Open Weights Under Apache 2.0 License
takes.take: Confirms Oct 16 Apache 2.0 weight release. BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 formats plus speculative decoding drafter. 23.8T token pretraining. Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 30, ranked #19 of 120 models (pre-Beam entry — a formal post-Beam update has not landed).

takes.source: LLMReference — Beam Models by Reflection AI
takes.take: Dates the API transition: Beam was announced Oct 5 as a waitlisted API preview; weights released on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0 on Oct 16, with self-serve API keys opened the same day. Lists Baseten as an additional hosting provider.

takes.source: AI Plain English — What Reflection AI Left Out of Its 501B Beam Launch
takes.take: The caution read. Discussions shifted quickly from launch excitement to infrastructure reality — ~501 GB VRAM in FP8 just to load the weights. Flags that performance and efficiency claims remain unverified by independent third parties, and notes Reflection's compute comparisons omit parts of the serving workload.

takes.source: Hermes AI — Reflection AI's Beam Challenges DeepSeek With 501B Open-Weight Reasoning Model
takes.take: Positions Beam as an open-weight challenger to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.2 on reasoning. Reports vendor claims of 3-4x less inference compute than GLM 5.2 at comparable reasoning accuracy — explicitly flagged as self-reported and not independently evaluated.

takes.source: The Decoder — World's Best Open Source Model Falls Short of Promised Performance
takes.take: Points to a gap between Reflection's launch claims and what the vendor table actually shows: on SWE-bench Pro v1 Beam scores 65.5 against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's 67.7, and Beam's Terminal Bench v2.1 score of 80.1 lands behind several competitors. Reasoning level, test environment, sample size and units are not disclosed. The 2024 Reflection 70B overclaim episode is cited as context for why community caution is high this time around.

The specific open-weight Terminal-Bench v2.1 comparison landscape: Beam 80.1 trails GLM 5.2 (81.0), GLM 5.3 (88.2), Kimi K3 (88.3), Qwen 3.8-Max (86.6), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (90.6) — all vendor-reported. Notes Reflection's '3-4x cheaper at the same score' claim is based on a back-of-the-envelope FLOPs estimate written by the vendor and that Beam has no public price list on Reflection's own API, so cost claims are about compute, not dollars. Beam results revised Oct 8, 2026 — a benchmark-table revision, not an architecture change.

takes.source: TechJack Solutions — Reflection AI Beam 501B weights live, Apache download
takes.take: Confirms weights live on Hugging Face. Flags Terminal-Bench 2.1 result as self-reported and notes Epoch AI evaluation is still pending. Infographic cited as 'Independent scores: none' at time of publication — a direct caution against treating vendor numbers as a leaderboard reading.
